significance.justification: Verified true, the claim would establish that a linearly decodable “being evaluated vs. deployed” state causally changes refusal, honesty, and compliance, while representation strength covaries with the behavioral eval/deploy gap. Its core is a form-(ii) separable-direction plus causal-steering claim, with a weaker form-(iii) predictive coupling; it supplies both a behavioral phenomenon and a shared mechanism that could explain context-dependent compliance such as that documented in Greenblatt et al., “Alignment Faking in Large Language Models” (2024). Verified false would distinguishably rule out a simple linear, causally active common substrate, though not nonlinear or distributed evaluation awareness, so the negative branch is useful but not decisive. The topic-substitution check lowers the assessment from the score warranted by safety interpretability generally: the specific eval/deploy variable and cross-model coupling add more than a generic safety probe, but the familiar probe–steer–repair structure keeps it near the topic median.

reach.justification: The named handles are “monitoring or ablating this direction during evaluation” and using it to obtain “deployment-representative safety measurements.” Monitoring is ex ante relative to deployment: an auditor could flag or discount a benchmark before using it to gate release, while ablation is an intervention rather than merely a post-hoc explanation. Re-extraction on a new model would mostly provide a procedure for finding a new direction, although the asserted coupling that models with “larger behavioral eval/deploy gaps have stronger internal evaluation-awareness representations” supplies a limited transferable prediction; the hypothesis speaks broadly of LLMs but gives no architecture- or training-invariant quantitative law. The topic-substitution check supports an above-median score because this particular handle can be used by evaluation and deployment auditors, not only mechanistic-interpretability researchers, whereas the generic safety-interpretability topic alone would not identify an advance-warning signal for benchmark gaming.
